rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding ~0.5 at% Hf to a dual-phase Al-Cr-Fe-Ni-Mo HEA, while the target paper added 4.2 at% Cr to a single-phase Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr BCC alloy. These are different kinds of interventions (different base alloy systems, different added elements, different phase targets).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies tensile testing at 800–1000 °C, whereas the target paper performed room-temperature compression testing. These are completely different temperature regimes and loading modes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes Hf-rich interfacial precipitates hindering grain boundary sliding and dislocation motion at high temperature. The target paper's mechanism is a dual mechanism of solid solution hardening from Cr and crack propagation hindrance from a reticulated Laves phase network. These are different general classes of mechanism (precipitation strengthening vs. solid solution + Laves phase toughening).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts ~40% improvement in high-temperature tensile strength and ductility. The target paper reports ~13.5% increase in yield strength and ~20.6% increase in fracture strain at room temperature. The property direction is similar (improvement in strength and ductility), but the magnitude, temperature, and loading mode differ substantially.
